technical.title: Example · Turn loose notes into a checklist
technical.body:
> This editable example uses demonstration code and data. Replace them with your own records.

## Context and goals
Turn three short notes into a checklist while preserving their meaning.

## Environment and prerequisites
- The input contains three text strings. No network or file writes are involved.
- The code is a reading example; it does not need to be executed.

## Implementation
```js
const notes = ["Describe the problem", "Record the process", "Check the result"];
const checklist = notes.map(text => `- [ ] ${text}`).join("\n");
```

## Verification
| Check | Example result |
| --- | --- |
| Number of items | 3 retained |
| Text | Matches the input |
| Order | Unchanged |

## Next steps
- [ ] Substitute your own problem.
- [ ] Add the actual environment and verification evidence.

website.body:

## Introduction
Some ideas become clearer as you write. Start with one useful paragraph, then add evidence and detail.

## Main content
### Begin with a specific question
Describe what the reader needs and the next step this page can help them take.

### Give each paragraph a purpose
Use headings for structure and lists for parallel points. The host website supplies navigation and the footer.

brief.title: Example · A small reading discussion proposal
brief.body:
> This is a demonstration proposal. The activity and its results have not occurred.

## Context
Try a small discussion to make it easier for readers to share questions from their reading.

## Goals
1. Each participant brings one specific question.
2. Keep discussion notes confirmed by the participants.

## Proposal and value
Read independently, discuss the questions, and record both agreements and unresolved points.

![Bundled artwork demonstrating an image in a proposal](/images/article-sample.png)

## Evidence
| Assumption | Evidence to collect |
| --- | --- |
| Questions shared in advance help preparation | Participant feedback |
| Small discussions make participation easier | Actual distribution of speaking time |

## Next steps
Confirm participants, timing and how notes will be kept. Write conclusions after the activity.

wechat.title: Example · Start with one small note
wechat.body:
> This editable example demonstrates a WeChat article layout. The text and image are sample content.

## Opening
Writing can begin with a small detail: a question from today, or something you finally understood.

## Main content
### Make the situation clear
Describe what happened, then add your observations. Give readers specific information and space to pause.

> Writing down a question can be the first step toward understanding it again.

![A layout example image bundled with the app](/images/article-sample.png)

### Leave room for the next step
- What has been confirmed?
- What still needs evidence?
- Where can the reader begin?

## Closing
Turn this example into your own story. Check copied content in a WeChat draft and on a phone.

community.title: Example · How do you organize quick notes?
community.body:
> This is a community post example. Adjust its length and formatting for the actual destination.

## The question
When loose notes accumulate, how do you find the one worth developing?

## Key points
- Add a title that makes sense later.
- Separate facts, questions and next steps.
- Keep sources so they can be checked.

## Context
This discussion concerns personal notes. These are example practices, without a measured comparison of their effectiveness.

## Related links
Add verified original sources here if you refer to someone else’s method.

## Join the discussion
Which step usually slows you down? Share one specific example.
